clue.text: Left inside after first of rustics makes witty remark

indicators.note: says the abbreviation goes within the word, straight after its opening letter

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin, first to leave, cracks a clever joke on the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of rustics' looks like a letter selection, but rustics is the whole word PEASANTRY, and L slips in after its first letter to give PLEASANTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light, humorous or polite remark made in conversation.

clue.text: Man captured, moving rook in advanced position on board

indicators.note: moving the piece in means shifting it into the middle of the other word

explanation.surface: A chess commentary: a man is taken, and the rook advances to a forward square.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture makes 'board' a chessboard, but it means on board ship: the PROW is its front.
explanation.definitionFit: The prow is the bow, the foremost part of a ship, so it is the most forward position aboard.

clue.text: Withdraw demand over time, right?

indicators.note: one thing placed over another covers it, so the first word goes round the following letters

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether they may take back a demand they made earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull or draw something out, which is a synonym of withdraw.

clue.text: Somehow hears about cold war tirade that allows the force to go in

definitions.text: that allows the force to go in

indicators.note: somehow suggests things done in an unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation

blocks.note: C for cold, as on a tap
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: Someone overhears a cold-war rant which somehow gives troops permission to invade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The force' looks military but is the police force, who need this document to enter premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A search warrant is a court order authorising police to enter and search a property.

clue.text: There are colonies where this practice is barely appropriate

definitions.text: There are colonies where this practice is barely appropriate

blocks.clueFragment: There are colonies where this practice is barely appropriate
blocks.note: surface reading: overseas colonies where some custom is only just suitable
setter's reading: colonies are naturist camps, where going bare is what is appropriate

explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonies' suggests empire and 'barely' means scarcely, but naturist colonies are camps where going without clothes is exactly fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudism is the practice of going about unclothed, typically in designated naturist colonies or camps.

clue.text: Place for relaxation or enjoyable activity, in short, on ship

explanation.surface: A cruise brochure: somewhere to unwind, or something fun, aboard the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A recliner is a chair whose back tilts so the sitter can lie back and rest.

clue.text: Two kinds of diamonds? Cool!

blocks.note: D is the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to be shown two types of diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase does double duty: diamonds as gems give the slang ICE, diamonds as a card suit give D.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced means chilled, cooled down to a low temperature, so it matches cool as an adjective.

clue.text: Be composed about relative informally appearing in court

indicators.note: things appearing in a place are inside it, so these letters sit within the court abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm about a family member turning up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Usually followed by 'of': to consist of is to be made up of.
explanation.definitionFit: To consist is to be made up or formed of parts, which is what being composed of means.

clue.text: What we need to survive — paper money?

explanation.surface: A question asking whether what keeps us alive is money in paper form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper money' reads as banknotes, but splits into a newspaper and a slang word for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily bread, from the Lord's Prayer, means the food or income needed to sustain life.

clue.text: Revealed room for improvement that's apparent

blocks.note: a secret that is out has been revealed
a hospital ward is a room where patients get better

explanation.surface: Someone has shown that clear scope for doing better exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room for improvement' is an idiom for shortcomings, but here it is read literally as a hospital room where people recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Outward means visible on the surface, as in outward appearances, so it matches apparent.

clue.text: Foreign character not favouring Italian wine

blocks.note: a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An outsider who dislikes the local red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine produced in the Tuscany region of Italy.

clue.text: In stupid way, securing degree, as expressed in particular language

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the first word holds the other inside

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly earned a qualification, judging by the way they phrase things.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking idiomatically means using the natural expressions peculiar to a given language.

clue.text: Ease of understanding bicycle, as it is spelt out

indicators.note: spelling out freshly suggests the letters being set down in a new arrangement

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: A simple explanation of how a bicycle works, laid out plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Accessibility of a text or idea is how readily people can grasp or follow it.

clue.text: In odd order, catalogued set

indicators.note: placed in a strange order means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A collection was catalogued in a peculiar sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a noun for the collection, but it is the verb, as jelly sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Coagulated means thickened from liquid to a solid or semi-solid state, as blood or jelly does.

clue.text: North American city has some power returning in old area

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the unit is read right to left

explanation.surface: A city regains some of its influence in a long-established district.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, in North America.

clue.text: Mathematician, for example, having come back and cracked theorem (not hard)

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the abbreviation is read backwards
says the pencil-grade letter for hard must be dropped
something cracked is broken up, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A mathematician, say, returns having solved a theorem that turned out not to be difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometer is a specialist in geometry, a branch of mathematics.

clue.text: Act legally when sheltering certain Europeans or Africans

indicators.note: to shelter someone is to keep them inside, so one word holds the other

explanation.surface: Acting within the law when giving refuge to people from Europe or Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Europeans or Africans' reads as one pair of refugees; the Europeans are wordplay and the Africans alone are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sudanese are the people of Sudan, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Large part of one's inheritance — get excited when it's cut

indicators.note: cutting a word short means losing its final letter

blocks.note: a gene is a unit of genetic inheritance
to rouse is to stir up or excite

explanation.surface: Someone gets agitated when most of their legacy is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large part' reads as a phrase, but 'Large' is the definition on its own, as in a generous helping.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous describes an ample or plentiful amount, as with a generous portion.

clue.text: Core family member having upset top couple and me, royally

indicators.note: upsetting the top two letters of a down word turns that pair upside down, swapping their order

explanation.surface: A central relative has offended the leading couple and the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central part or core around which other things gather.

clue.text: Ideal state without opiates, in part

indicators.note: says only a portion of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A perfect society would be partly drug-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia, from Thomas More's book, is an imagined perfect society or state.

clue.text: Piece of wood put on fire fell

blocks.note: to axe is to sack or fire someone

explanation.surface: A log is placed on a blaze, then it collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' reads as flames for the wood, but it means dismiss. 'Fell' looks past tense of fall but is the verb to knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: To poleaxe is to knock someone down with a heavy blow, as to fell them.

clue.text: Convenient American energy extracted from coal, say, and sent North

indicators.note: taking something out of a word removes it from that word
in a down entry north is upward, so the removed letter travels up to sit before the rest

blocks.note: coal is an example of fuel

explanation.surface: A handy American energy source, coal extracted and shipped north.
explanation.walkthrough: The energy letter is not discarded: it leaves the coal word and climbs the column, landing just above what remains of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Useful means handy or serviceable, which matches convenient as an adjective.

clue.text: Have no place for speaker I endlessly label lazy

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to lack is to have none
a dais, the raised platform a speaker stands on
to call is to name or label

explanation.surface: An unpopular speaker without a podium, unfairly branded idle again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackadaisical means lacking enthusiasm and effort, which is a lazy, careless attitude.

clue.text: Worst as verb, not as adjective

blocks.note: first meaning: the verb to worst, to defeat or get the better of someone
second meaning: as an adjective the answer is not worst but its exact opposite, the finest

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves lean on the opening word: as verbs the two words are synonyms, both meaning to defeat, while as adjectives they are opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to defeat or outdo them, the same as to worst them, though as adjectives best and worst are antonyms.

clue.text: Letters improperly providing one-sided support for board?

indicators.note: something done improperly is done wrongly, so the letters are put in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: Letters written improperly give a biased backing to the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests directors and 'one-sided support' bias, but a trestle table is a board resting on two trestles, each holding up one end.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame with splayed legs; a pair of them hold up a board to make a table, one at each side.

clue.text: Leaves family, almost before I mature

indicators.note: almost all of a word means its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone nearly walks out on their family before growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, departs, but it is the plural noun for what grows on trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage is the leaves of plants collectively.

clue.text: Something to eat in food I shared is here, sooner or later

indicators.note: says the answer sits inside the following words as a run of letters
says the same run of letters can be found once earlier and once later in the clue's wording

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A meal shared between friends will turn up eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden twice: early in 'food I shared' and later in 'shared is here', hence 'sooner or later'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared item of food, such as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Typo led men astray in preparation for battle

indicators.note: led astray means led off course, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A misprint in the orders sent soldiers the wrong way before the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Deployment is the positioning of troops ready for military action.
